entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Peter of Benevento was an Italian canon lawyer and cardinal who played a pivotal role in shaping the papacy's diplomatic relations during the Middle Ages. As papal legate, he represented Pope Innocent III at the Second Council of Lyon in 1274, where he negotiated with King Louis IX of France to secure an end to the Albigensian Crusade. This effort significantly contributed to the eventual resolution of the conflict and marked a turning point in the relationship between the Catholic Church and the French monarchy.

As cardinal, Peter of Benevento was instrumental in promoting the canonization of numerous saints, including the later pope, Urban IV. He also collaborated with other prominent cardinals, such as Berengar Frédol and Jacques de Vitry, to establish new church institutions and improve papal governance. His efforts helped pave the way for the papacy's increasing influence over European politics during this period.

Despite his significant contributions to the Church, Peter of Benevento's legacy has largely been overshadowed by that of other prominent figures from this era. Nevertheless, his work as a diplomat and administrator remains an important aspect of understanding the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized medieval European politics.

Like the intricate stone carvings adorning the cathedrals of southern Italy, Peter of Benevento's legacy is often subtle yet enduring, testifying to the power of steady, behind-the-scenes work in shaping the course of history.
